entities.summary:
East Asia is a vast and storied region spanning the modern-day countries of China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, and Taiwan. With a population of over 1.6 billion people, it is one of the most populous regions on Earth. The earliest known civilizations in East Asia emerged during the Yangshao Culture (c. 5000-2000 BCE), which laid the groundwork for subsequent cultures such as the Shang Dynasty (16th-11th centuries BCE) and the Zhou Dynasty (1046–256 BCE).

The Silk Road, a network of ancient trade routes, connected East Asia to the rest of the world, facilitating the exchange of goods, ideas, and technologies. The region was also home to some of the most influential philosophical traditions in human history, including Buddhism and Taoism.

In recent centuries, East Asia has played a crucial role in shaping modern world history. The Opium Wars (1839–1842, 1856–1860) forced China to open its markets to European trade, while Japan's Meiji Restoration (1868–1877) transformed it into a modern industrialized nation.

Today, East Asia continues to be an important player in global affairs. The region is home to some of the world's most populous countries, including China and India, and is increasingly influential in international trade, politics, and culture.
